Good, I reverted. Now let me think about this more carefully.

The requirement says "Left- and center-aligned search operations must consume input up to the next space character."

When doing a search (not an exact parse), for left-aligned ('<') and center-aligned ('^'), the pattern should stop at the next space instead of consuming all padding characters.

For left-align '<', the current pattern is `(.+?) *` which matches content followed by any number of spaces. But we want it to stop at the first space after the content.

For center-align '^', the current pattern is ` *(.+?) *` which matches leading spaces, content, then trailing spaces. We want it to stop at the first space.

Actually, looking at this from a different angle: when searching, we want to match the value but not consume extra whitespace. So maybe we should use a non-greedy match that stops at space.

Let me look at how search works vs parse in this library...
